title: Install a tool-less Open Rack V3 IT support bracket from inside the frame
objective: Orient one Open Rack V3 IT support bracket inside the rack, align its tool-less mounting features with the specified frame cutouts, engage and lock the bracket without external access, and leave it seated without interfering with adjacent brackets or chassis space.
skills: bimanual support of an elongated load-bearing part
clearance management around adjacent rack hardware
success_conditions: Blocked pending the referenced OCP CAD/drawing and a concrete bracket design. At minimum, a valid rubric would require all documented tool-less mounting features to be engaged from inside the frame, correct OpenU registration, self-support after release, no interference with nearby brackets or chassis envelopes, and no permanent deformation. No hook count, insertion motion, latch state, force threshold, or success claim may be invented from the currently acquired text.
industrial_value: The Open Rack Meta Frame V3 specification defines these brackets as the shelf support for IT gear, requires tool-less direct mounting, inside-frame serviceability, and substantial load capacity. This establishes industrial relevance, but not yet an executable manipulation sequence.
dexterity: Potentially high because a long load-bearing bracket must be registered and latched within a constrained rack interior. The exact dexterity cannot be asserted until the referenced bracket CAD and drawing reveal its real mounting features.

asset_plan: Do not begin task construction from the prose alone. First obtain the exact OCP collateral named in section 12.8, confirm its license, select one bracket revision, and extract its mounting-feature geometry and rack interface without mixing revisions. Then build an independent rigid PhysX model, validate every engagement feature, incorrect-level rejection, self-support, adjacent-clearance, overload behavior, and reset repeatability before considering YAM integration.
risk: Blocked and not selected. The acquired specification proves purpose, access direction, tool-less mounting, and load requirements, but the referenced CAD/drawing is not present in the acquired package. The actual hooks, tabs, latches, insertion trajectory, dimensions, and retention mechanics are therefore unknown. Treating this as build-ready would require invented geometry and success criteria; it may also be semantically close to other rack-rail or shelf-support installation tasks.
